Fields: id, brand, product, species, life_stage, form(dry|wet, added for ranges), kcal_per_100g, protein_pct, fat_pct, moisture_pct, fibre_pct, source_url, source_date, label_year.

baseline.what: Home-made 30-line Node validator (runs/01-catalogue/baseline.mjs): required keys present, numbers are numbers, strings are strings. JSON input.
baseline.note: Only the structural fault (missing source_date) is structural; the other 9 are semantic/range/cross-field faults by design, so the team's claim of 8/10 on tabular faults does not transfer to this fixture.

candidate_default.config: Ajv: schema-default.json = type/required/enum/format(uri,date)/additionalProperties only, Ajv2020 strict+allErrors+ajv-formats. Frictionless: tableschema-default.json = field types + required + enum + date type/uri format, `frictionless validate catalogue.csv --schema ... --trusted --json`.

candidate_tuned.config: Ajv: schema-tuned.json adds minimum/maximum on every number (kcal 50-600, protein 3-60, fat 1-40, moisture 3-90, fibre 0-15, label_year 2022-2026), if/then/else on form (dry kcal 200-600 & moisture<=14; wet kcal 50-200 & moisture>=60), id pattern, plus TWO custom keywords registered in ajv-run.mjs: proteinGteFat (row rule, applied under then: for dry) and uniqueKey:'id' (array-level, because uniqueItems compares whole objects). Frictionless: tableschema-tuned.json adds the same minimum/maximum, unique:true + primaryKey on id, pattern; checklist-tuned.json adds two row-constraint checks (simpleeval formulas): `form != 'dry' or protein_pct >= fat_pct` and the per-form kcal/moisture ranges. Why: a type-only schema cannot see magnitudes; ranges are the only schema-level lever against unit faults, and cross-row/cross-field rules need custom logic.

ajv.note: 15 error objects for 10 faults: kcal maximum fires from both the base property and the then: branch, and Ajv adds an 'if' wrapper error per failing branch (wrapper filters keyword 'if').

frictionless.note: 13 errors for 10 faults: F6 reported twice (unique-error + primary-key), F1/F4 twice (constraint maximum + row-constraint).

custom_logic_ajv: F6 duplicate id (custom keyword uniqueKey; JSON Schema has no cross-item key uniqueness)
F9 protein>=fat (custom keyword proteinGteFat; JSON Schema has no cross-property comparison)
custom_logic_frictionless: F9 protein>=fat (row-constraint check in checklist; F6 is native via unique/primaryKey)
custom_in_both: F9 (cross-field row rule). Unit-label faults F1-F3 were caught ONLY because their magnitude fell outside the range; the probe (runs/01-catalogue/probe/) shows a kJ value of 188 on a wet row passes both tuned configs with exit 0 -> unit faults with in-range magnitude are invisible to both tools and need a source-side unit field or a plausibility rule (e.g. Atwater kcal estimate from protein/fat vs declared kcal).

limits: Both tools at defaults are no better than the baseline on this fixture (2/10 vs 1/10): everything useful came from ranges and custom rules, which the team must author and maintain.
Unit-label faults are invisible to any schema when the wrong-unit magnitude stays inside the plausible range (probe: 188 kJ on a wet row passes both). Ranges catch only gross unit errors.

Ajv: JSON Schema cannot express duplicate ids across array items (uniqueItems compares whole objects) nor cross-field comparisons; both needed addKeyword (~6 lines each). Strict mode rejected then/else subschemas lacking 'type' on first try.
Ajv reports duplicate error objects (base + then branch + 'if' wrapper) for one fault; a wrapper must dedupe/filter.

Frictionless: CLI refused relative '../' and absolute paths with 'path ... is not safe' until --trusted was passed; the Python runtime adds 73 MB and a second toolchain for a Node team; CLI start-up ~0.4 s per run; row-constraint formulas are simpleeval strings (no editor support, errors only at runtime).

Frictionless validates the CSV, Ajv the JSON; the calculator consumes JSON, so Frictionless would validate a sibling file unless the JSON is converted (Frictionless can read JSON arrays too, not measured).
Runtimes measured on a shared 4-vCPU box with other trials running; 40 rows is tiny, numbers are start-up dominated.
trials.verdict: ADOPT (Ajv 8.20.0 tuned schema + two custom keywords); WATCH (Frictionless 5.21.0: equal recall, but Python toolchain and no advantage for a Node team)
trials.reason: Baseline catches 1/10; Ajv defaults 2/10 and Frictionless defaults 2/10 with 0 false positives; both tuned configs catch 10/10 with 0 false positives on 40 clean control rows. Ajv costs 3.2 MB / 3 s install, pure JS, 0.18 s per run and lives in the Node repo the calculator already uses; Frictionless matches recall but needs a 73 MB Python venv, --trusted, and 0.52 s per run. 6 of the 10 faults are caught purely by min/max ranges, 2 (dup id, protein>=fat) need custom keywords in Ajv, and in-range unit faults are not detectable by either.
trials.wrapper: runs/01-catalogue/wrapper-sketch.mjs (checks/catalogue.mjs; exit 0 on catalogue-clean.json, 1 on catalogue.json with 10 rows flagged, 2 on missing file)
do_not_adopt_notes: Do not adopt Frictionless for this use: identical recall to Ajv after tuning, but adds Python 3.13 + 41 packages (73 MB) to a Node-on-Windows team, needs --trusted for normal paths, and validates CSV rather than the JSON the calculator reads.
Do not rely on schema defaults alone: type/required/enum caught only F5 and F7, which is no measurable gain over the baseline (1/10).

Ranges are not unit detection: F1-F3 passed as 'caught' only because 1500, 280 and 0.1 fall outside plausible bounds; a kJ value of 188 on a wet row passed both tuned validators (probe). Add a unit column at the source or an Atwater plausibility rule to close that gap.

Why: constraints express 'non-literal RHS' and 'unescaped' which plain patterns cannot; two tree-sitter-php quirks had to be worked around (a pattern with a literal comma needs >=2 args so both arities are listed; a captured argument is the `argument` wrapper node, so constraints use `has`).
candidate_tuned.note: 10 findings = exactly the 10 seeded locations. S3 is caught syntactically (echo of a bare variable), NOT by flow analysis: ast-grep has no taint mode, so `echo $count` of a safe integer would be flagged the same way (WordPress coding standards flag it too).

semgrep_ce.config: runs/02-patterns/semgrep/rules-tuned.yml (8 rules): pattern-either for eval/alias (const|let|var $A = eval, $A = eval), $G[$K](...) with metavariable-regex on $K (constant folding turns 'ev'+'al' into a string so pattern-not $G["..."] hides it); innerHTML with pattern-not "..."; setTimeout/setInterval with metavariable-regex on $CB; php-echo-tainted-request = mode: taint ($_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST/$_COOKIE/$_SERVER[...] source, esc_*/wp_kses*/sanitize_*/intval/absint/rawurlencode sanitizers, echo/print sink); php-echo-unescaped-var (metavariable-regex: bare variable/property/index); php-wpdb-interpolated-sql = mode: taint (any function parameter -> $wpdb->query/get_* without $wpdb->prepare/esc_sql/intval/absint), because metavariable-regex could not see the content of a PHP interpolated string.
semgrep_ce.note: 12 findings on 10 seeded locations: lazy-eval.js:3 reported twice (two eval sub-patterns) and search.php:13 twice (syntactic + taint rule). Taint genuinely tracked $_GET['q'] -> $q -> echo $q across two statements, which ast-grep cannot do. Invalid PHP patterns in this version: '(int) ...' and '"..." . ...' (rule parse errors). CE JSON output hides matched lines/metavars ('requires login'), so results carry only path/line/rule.

limits: ast-grep is purely syntactic: no data flow. 'echo $var' is flagged whether or not $var is safe; '$sql = "... $id"; $wpdb->query($sql)' (variable holding an interpolated string) is NOT caught by either ast-grep rule.

ast-grep PHP quirks (tree-sitter-php): patterns with a literal comma need >=2 args (list both arities); the captured call argument is the `argument` wrapper, so constraints must use `has:`; <?= $x ?> short-echo not covered by the `echo $X` pattern (untested).
The php-echo-unescaped allow-list of escaping/i18n function names is hand-maintained; a new helper (e.g. a theme's own esc wrapper) must be added or it is flagged.

Semgrep registry (p/..., --config auto) is unreachable through this proxy: only local rules measured. Without --disable-version-check a run took 98.8 s (version check against semgrep.dev hangs until timeout).
Semgrep CE 1.182.1: metavariable-regex does not see the text of a PHP interpolated string; JSON output omits matched lines and metavariable values ('requires login').
Semgrep on Windows: wheel exists on PyPI but was not executed here; needs Python >=3.10 on each machine (the team runs Node).
Runtimes measured on a 4-vCPU box shared with other trials; all are sub-second except Semgrep's ~1.8-2 s Python startup.

trials.reason: ast-grep tuned finds 8/8 seeded defects (10/10 locations) with 0 false positives on the 4 controls and 0 extras, vs grep 5/8 with 3 of 4 controls flagged; it runs in 0.02 s, installs in 4 s / 106 MB as a plain npm devDependency with win32-x64 binaries, and the rules are 7 small YAML files. Ratio is a stem-level number: it says nothing about spectral masking; +6 dB is a rule of thumb, not an intelligibility measure.
ebur128 'Peak' line is true peak only with peak=true (4x oversampled); AAC encoding raised sample-peak-limited material by up to ~3 dB TP in this trial, so limit at <= -3 dBFS before encoding.
Synthetic fixtures (espeak voice, synth bed), 25 s; real TTS voices and licensed beds not tested; no Windows run (hosts for the static builds are refused from the sandbox).

Dynamic regions must be enumerated as selectors (Playwright mask); the mask box follows the element box, so a masked element whose size depends on the dynamic text needs a fixed size or its container masked (we mask the whole [data-dynamic] bar).

Full-page screenshots of different height (U1) make pixelmatch throw; the harness/wrapper pads with white. Fixed in-wrapper, but the reported bbox then covers everything below the shift, which is correct but not 'the 2px margin'.

'Segoe UI' resolves to Inter via fontconfig on this Linux box; cross-OS font metrics differ, so baselines must be captured on the same OS/browser build as the check (Windows vs Linux screenshots will never match).

Runtimes have shared-CPU noise (4 vCPU, concurrent trials).
